newsitem.title: COLOMBIA: Colombia's imports fall 1.3 percent in 1996.
newsitem.headline: Colombia's imports fall 1.3 percent in 1996.

text.p: Colombia's imports fell 1.3 percent to $13.6 billion CIF (cost, insurance and freight) in 1996 compared with 1995, the National Tax and Excise Directorate said in a report Monday.
The value of imports in 1995 was $13.8 billion, the report said.
Imports of industrial goods dropped 3.4 percent while imports for the mining sector grew 31.8 percent and for agriculture increased 30.7 percent, the report stated.

Imports of raw materials and unfinished goods were up 2.2 percent compared with 1995 and accounted for more than 45 percent of total imports. Imports of capital goods and construction materials rose 6.5 percent while imports of consumer goods fell by 25.3 percent and accounted for 14.1 percent of total imports.
Colombia's main trading partner continues to be the United States. It supplied 38 percent of the country's imports, valued at $5.1 billion in 1996 -- a 2.6 percent increase from 1995.
Venezuela, Colombia's second leading trading partner, sent goods worth $1.3 billion to the country last year -- a 5.5 percent drop compared with 1995.
Colombia's Tax and Excise Directorate collected 2.5 trillion pesos (about $2.5 billion) in import duty in 1996, according to the official report.
